thread.document:
I was struggling to understand SSMs, the jump from RNNs to continuous-time systems to convolutions felt disconnected. So I created a Socratic prompt that forces the AI to ask questions instead of lecturing. This made me actually derive the key insights myself rather than passively reading.

The Prompt:

"You are a Socratic tutor helping me understand State-Space Models (S4, Mamba) for CS182 (graduate deep learning at Berkeley).

RULES:

Ask me questions BEFORE explaining. Don't lecture—guide me to discover.

Build intuition FIRST with analogies, THEN introduce math.

Check my understanding at each step before proceeding.

Be honest if something is uncertain or an open research question.

After the core content, stress-test me with "what would break if..." questions.

STRUCTURE:

Phase 1: Check what I know about RNNs and Transformers (prerequisites)

Phase 2: Intuition for what problem SSMs solve and why

Phase 3: The continuous-time formulation and discretization (with pauses for questions)

Phase 4: The convolution trick (why we can parallelize training)

Phase 5: Limitations and how Mamba addresses them

Phase 6: Common misconceptions students have

Phase 7: Give me 3 self-assessment questions (conceptual, mathematical, reasoning)

Context: I understand RNNs, vanishing gradients, and attention. I haven't worked with differential equations in ML before.

Start with Phase 1."

Key Realization

The AI had me expand a linear recurrence manually:

h₁ = A·h₀ + B·x₁ h₂ = A²h₀ + AB·x₁ + B·x₂ h₃ = A³h₀ + A²B·x₁ + AB·x₂ + B·x₃

From this I realized: it's just a convolution with kernel [B, AB, A²B, ...]. Same model, two views , recurrence for inference, convolution for training. Deriving it myself made it click way better than lecture.

Analysis

What worked well:

Socratic approach forced active thinking instead of passive reading

Built intuition before math (why SSMs exist → how they work)

Good misconceptions section — I would've said "O(n) training" but it's actually O(n log n) due to FFT

Where it was incomplete:

HiPPO mentioned but not explained mathematically

Parallel scan (Mamba's trick) glossed over

No code examples

What I now understand:

Linear recurrence = convolution (parallelizable via FFT)

Continuous-time formulation enables principled initialization

S4 = fixed kernel (LTI), Mamba = input-dependent (selective)

Learnable Δ = learnable temporal resolution
